title: Kill Bill: Vol. 1
events_chronological: The Bride, a member of the Deadly Viper Assassination Squad, leaves the life for the child she is carrying and plans a wedding in an El Paso chapel under a new name.
Bill and the Vipers walk into the wedding rehearsal and massacre everyone in the chapel.
Bill shoots the Bride through the head, and she survives in a coma.
O-Ren Ishii, whose parents were murdered in front of her as a child, kills the boss responsible at eleven and grows up to be a top assassin.
O-Ren takes the Tokyo underworld by beheading a rival at a council meeting, and rules it with the schoolgirl killer Gogo Yubari and the lawyer Sofie Fatale.
Elle Driver comes to the hospital to kill the comatose Bride with a syringe and is called off by Bill at the last moment.
For four years the orderly Buck sells the comatose Bride's body to visitors.
The Bride wakes, kills Buck and his customer, and finds her belly flat and her baby gone.
She lies in the back of Buck's truck for thirteen hours until she can move her toes.
The Bride writes out her list of five names and drives to Vernita Green's house in Pasadena.
The two fight through the kitchen, break off when Vernita's small daughter comes home from school, and the Bride kills Vernita with a thrown knife in front of the child.
The Bride flies to Okinawa and talks the retired swordsmith Hattori Hanzo into making her a blade to kill his own former student, Bill.
In Tokyo the Bride cuts Sofie Fatale's arm off outside the House of Blue Leaves and sends her to Bill as a message.
The Bride kills Gogo Yubari and then fights her way through the Crazy 88 across the restaurant.
The Bride duels O-Ren in the snow garden and takes off the top of her skull.
She interrogates the maimed Sofie in the boot of a car and leaves her alive to tell Bill everything.
Bill asks Sofie whether the Bride knows that her daughter is still alive.
syuzhet_notes: The film is cut into numbered chapters that ignore chronology outright. Told-order bullet 1 is the shooting everything hangs on, played before anything that explains it; bullet 2 opens Chapter One with what is chronologically the second-to-last killing on the list; and bullets 4-9 then reach back to the massacre and the four-year coma. Told-order bullets 10-11 are an animated flashback covering O-Ren's entire life, dropped in immediately before she dies.
fabula_notes: Vol. 1 shows the El Paso massacre only in fragments - a black-and-white aftermath and a few seconds of the rehearsal - so the events leading up to it are partly inferred. That the Bride's daughter survived is withheld until the film's last line, which retroactively changes the meaning of her waking in bullet 8.
